requirements.evidence: Both tables match the spec: entities slug unique 'entities_slug_unique' plus softDeletes (2026_10_29_043319_create_entities_table.php:6-9). Memberships have FKs with cascadeOnDelete, role default 'employee', storedAs owner_seq and both named unique indexes (2026_10_29_043320_create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-27). Contract is covered: Entity getRouteKeyName/memberships/users/owner (app/Models/Entity.php:23-54); EntityMembership cast + #[Scope] owner/admin/employee + entity/user (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:23-70); UserRole::manageable (app/Models/UserRole.php:16-19); User::memberships/entities/membershipFor (app/Models/User.php:35-58); factories with states. Policy rules match the task, e.g. `if ($membership->role === UserRole::Owner) return false;` then self-removal or manager (app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:27-34).

conventions.evidence: Authorization lives in app/Policies, and the test checks the policies are auto-discovered (tests/Feature/EntityPolicyTest.php:23-30). Mass assignment is deliberate via #[Fillable([...])], following User.php's existing attribute style. Both migrations have a reversible down(). docs/database-schema.md is updated to drop owner_membership_id and describe owner_seq and the policies, and CHANGELOG.md gets an [Unreleased] entry. Code was written test-first with Pest feature tests. No Actions are needed because the task adds no domain writes.

security.evidence: Non-members get nothing: every check goes through `$user->membershipFor($entity->id)?->role`, so a null membership returns false (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:43-50). Membership checks are scoped to the target's own entity_id (app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:39-42), and cross-entity outsiders are tested (EntityPolicyTest.php:93-101). The owner membership can never be deleted. Fillable is explicit. There is no user-facing input or output in this change.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/EntityModelTest.php covers columns, index names, enum values, route key, factory slug uniqueness, duplicate slug, soft delete, the DB-level role default, scopes, relations, membershipFor null, the second-owner rejection on insert and on promotion, multiple owners across entities and the duplicate member. tests/Feature/EntityPolicyTest.php uses datasets for every role and non-members on both policies, plus owner-membership deletion, self-removal and cross-entity admins. Two small gaps: no test for the cascade on entity delete (only the user cascade, EntityModelTest.php:142-147), and none for assignRole/delete when the actor is an admin of the same entity targeting another admin.

simplicity.evidence: Minimal code. Each policy has one private helper (roleIn/isManager), owner() reuses hasOne()->where(...), and membershipFor is a one-line query. There are no extra layers or speculative abstractions.

readability.evidence: Clear names and short methods. PHPDoc generics on relations match Laravel style. A comment explains the NULL-in-unique-index trick (create_entity_memberships_table.php:19-20). No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: The diff only touches models, policies, factories, migrations, tests, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md. There are no routes, session, middleware or UI. The docs edit is the update the task asked for; it also drops the unimplemented `locale_default` line from the entities diagram (docs/database-schema.md:34).

issues.explanation: The memberships cascade is only tested for user deletion; the entity FK cascade (on force delete) is not tested.
Removing the `locale_default` column from the proposed entities diagram goes slightly beyond replacing owner_membership_id; that planned column is now undocumented.
The global helper function `memberOf` in a Pest file can clash with same-named helpers in other test files; tests/Pest.php or a namespaced helper would be safer.

review.summary: The change adds the entities and entity_memberships migrations (including the generated owner_seq column with a unique index that enforces one owner per entity), the Entity/EntityMembership/UserRole models, the User relations, factories, both policies, thorough Pest tests and the matching schema docs and changelog entry. It meets the full contract and the project conventions with lean, readable code. The only gaps are small test omissions and a minor doc trim, so I would approve it with nits.
